memory_update.text: VECO is the strongest US-listed underfollowed candidate for the compound-semiconductor epitaxy/process-tool node because it has disclosed $250M+ of InP laser manufacturing equipment orders tied to optical interconnect demand.
AIXNY/Aixtron should remain a reference leader for MOCVD arsenide/phosphide tools, but verify US OTC listing, liquidity, and current market-cap bucket before using it in later dashboard layers.
LITE and COHR are not pure equipment plays but are essential demand anchors: their InP laser and 800G/1.6T optical capacity ramps validate tool demand for Veeco and Aixtron.

Need next-layer search for smaller metrology, in-situ epitaxy monitoring, specialty materials, precursor, wafer, and inspection suppliers tied to MOCVD/InP laser yield; these may be more obscure than the direct toolmakers.

VECO should be added to the AI optical connectivity upstream equipment universe as the cleanest US-listed direct compound semiconductor tool candidate; verify exact AI/datacom InP order exposure before promotion to later layers.
AXTI should be tracked as an adjacent InP/GaAs substrate chokepoint tied to the same laser/epitaxy capacity expansion, but it is a materials candidate rather than an epitaxy-tool candidate.

ONTO should be tracked as an adjacent metrology/inspection/process-control candidate for compound semiconductor and photonics yield, with evidence still needed for material revenue exposure to InP/laser/datacom customers.
Lumentum's reported Aixtron G10-AsP MOCVD orders are a strong demand-anchor signal that AI optical connectivity demand is moving upstream into InP laser and detector manufacturing tools.

Aixtron appears central to the node but is not a primary candidate in this US-listed pass; future non-US or ADR-inclusive passes should map AIXA/AIXNY, AMEC, LayTec-private exposure if accessible, and other MOCVD/metrology suppliers.

VECO is the highest-priority US-listed underfollowed candidate for the compound semiconductor epitaxy/tools node because it has explicit 2026 evidence of $250M+ InP laser manufacturing equipment orders tied to AI optical infrastructure.
AXTI is not an equipment supplier but should remain in the universe as a second-order InP substrate chokepoint and demand validator for epitaxy and laser tool capacity.
AIIXY/Aixtron is the key non-US reference peer for MOCVD/compound semiconductor deposition tools; keep it as a benchmark for backlog duration, end-market mix, and competitive share versus VECO.

Need a focused follow-up search for US-listed metrology, inspection, test, gas delivery, precursor, and service suppliers specifically tied to InP/GaAs laser epitaxy; current evidence is strongest for tool vendors and substrate suppliers, weaker for testing/certification gates.

VECO is the highest-priority US-listed candidate for the compound-semiconductor epitaxy tools node because it has direct public evidence of InP laser manufacturing equipment orders and MOCVD/InP epitaxy relevance.

AEHR should be tracked as an adjacent optical-interconnect reliability/testing chokepoint rather than a direct epitaxy-tool name; survival depends on evidence of multi-customer silicon photonics order broadening.
ONTO is a metrology/process-control adjacency for compound semiconductor and photonics manufacturing; direct AI optical interconnect customer proof is still needed.
ICHR remains a speculative shadow candidate until direct supply relationships with MOCVD/compound semiconductor tool OEMs or datacom laser capacity customers are verified.

The node may split into three research subnodes: direct epitaxy/process tools, photonics reliability/test, and metrology/subsystem suppliers. Later layers should avoid mixing their evidence thresholds.
